detailed_description:
Angular stylised 3D animation, brush-stroke texture, Horsell, Surrey, 1894, last daylight from the left, black shadows.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:06. The shot opens on an insert on the pale greenish afterglow above the sand: the polished silver disk at the apex of the thin jointed mast with its wobbling mirror, tilted over on its short yoke, the top joint of the dark bronze rod under it, the sky bare behind them; only that object and what touches it is in frame. The camera is on the heather looking out over the heaps at the sky, a 300mm lens. The last daylight stands low from the LEFT beyond the rod. At the first frame the pale greenish-blue afterglow fills the frame from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge and from the TOP edge to the BOTTOM edge. The polished silver disk stands at the CENTRE LEFT, a fifth of the height of the frame. The shot is inside this place: Horsell Common at twilight in 1894: knee-deep purple-brown heather and dark furze reading near-black, two young Scots pines standing black against the sky, a low raw ring of flung yellow sand round the crater a hundred yards off with a thin jointed mast standing above it. The camera tracks sideways to the right, a truck with small amplitude along the sky until the disk stands at the centre of the picture, travelling a finger's breadth as the disk swings round on its yoke and wobbles as it turns, the rim catching the afterglow once each turn, from 00:00 to 00:03. At 00:03 the rod under it leans a thumb's width and the disk goes on turning above it, and the lean continues to the last frame of the shot. By 00:06 the camera is tracking through the last frame, and the action continues with it.

overall_soundscape: The ambience of Horsell Common at twilight in 1894: knee-deep purple-brown heather and dark furze reading near-black runs under the whole take: its own air, the surfaces underfoot and the fabric of the place around it. Cloth, boots and the small sounds of hands on wood, glass and iron carry the physical action throughout.
